summary: Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Bokar Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, whom he also taught.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (1879–1941) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Shenphen Nangwa and Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen (~1897–1901), and taught figures such as Chatral Sangye Dorje.
Khenpo Nüden studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He also taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Lama Zolpa Trinlé, and the 16th Karmapa (~1960–1981). He served at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and Pullahari Monastery (1992).

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under teachers including Jetsun Lochen Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970), and at the University of Virginia (~1978–1980).

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rumtek Monastery and under numerous teachers. He held teaching positions at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was a scholar in Tibetology. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen, and taught Yeshi Donden among others.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie (attested 2015), and studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and the University of Freiburg (1920). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1911–1945), Hokkaido University (1947–1951), and Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kien T. Le works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MDiv at Harvard University (2023–2026) and became a PhD student at Indiana University Bloomington in 2026.
Kim Gutschow specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held positions at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).
Kim Lam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who has held posts at Deakin University and Western Sydney University, where she served as Research Officer.

Kim Plofker (born 1964) is an Indology and history scholar who earned her PhD at Brown University (~1989–1995) under David Pingree. She worked at MIT and Utrecht University, and held multiple professorial posts at Union College (2007–2019).

Kimberley C. Patton (born 1958) is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992). She held faculty posts at Harvard University (~1991–2000 and ~2000) and was an associate at ASCSA (1991).

Kimiaki Tanaka (born 1955) works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford, and held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Beijing Center for Japanese Studies, and Keio University.

Kimmo Koskenniemi (born 1945) works in computational linguistics. He earned an MSc at the University of Helsinki (1964–1967), where he later served as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2013) and directed the BAULT research community (~2000–2005).
